issue_text: childEvidencePassed treats a child task as having passing acceptance evidence if any evidence line mentioning the child ID also contains the bare substring "ok" (line 195) or "pass" (line 192). Because these are unanchored strings.Contains checks over lowercased text, common failure words contain them: "broke", "broken", "look"/"lookup", "took" all contain "ok"; "bypassed", "surpassed" contain "pass". So an evidence line like "task-1 broke CI, reverting" or "task-1 was bypassed" is accepted as passing, and missingChildEvidence drops that child from the missing list.

servicePathPattern = `(?i)(service|controller|worker|client)\.(go|js|ts|tsx|jsx|py|rb)$|(?i)(service|controller|worker|client)`. The second alternative is an unanchored bare-word match, which subsumes the first (any path matching the anchored `<word>.<ext>$` alternative also contains the word). The intended extension anchoring in the first alternative is therefore dead, and missingServiceInventoryCoverage fires on ANY changed path containing service/controller/worker/client as a substring, regardless of extension or role: e.g. docs/client-guide.md, config/worker.yaml, and internal/client_helper.go all match, raising a blocking "Missing service inventory update" for docs and config files.

violatesNoEvalIntent uses strings.Contains(evidence, "eval(") on the lowercased diff/child bodies, with no word boundary. This matches inside longer identifiers: "retrieval(input)" contains "eval(". So when the epic body states a no-eval intent ("without executing"/"no eval"/"avoid eval"), a diff that legitimately calls something like retrieval(...) triggers a false "Epic intent drift" blocker. The deterministic security lint in taskdone.go deliberately uses `\beval\s*\(` to avoid exactly this; the epic path does not.
